question: A capacitor allows AC to pass through a circuit, while a reverse biased p-n junction allows only a very small current. Explain the difference in the mechanism of current flow in the two cases.

options.A: Capacitive current involves continuous barrier crossing by majority carriers, while diode current is due to alternating dielectric displacement.
options.B: Capacitive current is limited by a widening depletion region, whereas reverse diode current is sustained by continuous charging and discharging.
options.C: Capacitive current is due to changing voltage, while reverse diode current is restricted by the p-n junction barrier.
options.D: Both currents arise from identical mechanisms governed solely by minority carrier drift across a shared dielectric medium.
